H_hierarchical.evidence: The paper defines five flat RIS states: train_not_CS, train_tries_CS, train_in_CS, train_away_CS, and train_out_CS; no parent/child or composite state structure is described.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Table 1 uses multi-variable Boolean conditions such as switch & !Sensor2 & sensor1, states=train_not_CS & switch & sensor2 & sensor1, and AG!(sensor1 & sensor2 & switch).

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: Transitions/states drive concrete outputs: close/open gate1 and gate2, turn alarm lights on/flashing/off, and turn the whistle on/off.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: The paper includes TMR fault masking for D flip-flop faults, but the RIS control FSM itself has no explicit recovery transition or global fault-to-safe-state escape path.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: State names are introduced in Section 3.2, while actuator behavior appears in the Section 3.1 scenario list, Table 1 properties, and later hardware equations/results.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as railway interlocking, safety-critical interlocking zone, and safe state imply domain constraints about conflict prevention and fail-safe behavior.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: The state list mostly gives state meanings; actions such as gates closed, red lights flashing, and whistle on/off are narrated elsewhere and must be attributed back to states.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: The formal properties contain Boolean-composed multi-variable guards, especially sensor1 & sensor2 & switch and switch & !Sensor2 & sensor1.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: No composite state or parent-state entry/during/exit behavior is specified.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: Fault tolerance is handled by hardware majority voting; the NL does not define a from-any-state fault transition to a safe controller state.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: There is no composite-state initialization or pseudo-state chain.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: The paper has several Boolean-composed guard/property formulas and explicitly reports that the sensor1/sensor2 mutual-exclusion property was initially falsified and required refinement.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: No explicit cross-cutting transition over multiple substates or parent-level continuous monitor is declared.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: Outputs are concrete actuators: gates, lights, and whistle, not abstract publish/log/notify actions.

key_nl_quotes: The finite state machine will transition into a safe state in which the two gates will be opened.
one_line_pitch: A flat but evidence-rich railway interlocking EFSM that stresses multi-variable Boolean guards and actuator attribution across prose, properties, and hardware equations.
rationale: This is a meaningful stress case for guard extraction and concrete transition-action attribution: the controller has multiple Boolean-composed sensor/switch conditions and several actuator outputs. Its baseline difficulty is high because state names, actions, and formal properties are distributed across sections and rely on interlocking/safe-state terminology. However, it lacks hierarchical structure and explicit global recovery transitions, so it is better as a backup sample than a top candidate.
